what_was_unfinished_and_is_now_done.the_law: see every important or valuable thing: what it is and how valuable it is. Stated twenty times.
what_was_unfinished_and_is_now_done.what_i_had_been_doing: answering with a seven-item list. That is a highlight reel, not a census, and it does not satisfy the law.
what_was_unfinished_and_is_now_done.what_i_did: enumerated the entire population of written claims -- every JSON governance record -- and priced each one by the weight it can bear
what_was_unfinished_and_is_now_done.why_this_population_is_the_right_one: this repository writes down every claim it makes as a governance record with a status, a date and usually hard_nonclaims. The claims are therefore finite and enumerable, which is what makes a census possible at all.

PROVEN.meaning: declares a passed or independently-run check

ACTIVE.meaning: a live route or mechanism, not a completed proof

REFUSED.meaning: a fail-closed outcome -- asserts that something did NOT work

the_pricing_rule_and_why_it_is_ordered_t.order: PROVEN > ACTIVE > REFUSED > CANDIDATE > RETRACTED > UNCLASSIFIED
the_pricing_rule_and_why_it_is_ordered_t.why: a documented failure is evidence -- it narrows the space of what can be true, and it cost something real to obtain. A candidate is a sentence about what might be true and costs nothing. An inventory that ranks proposals above refusals is upside down, and most inventories are upside down.
the_pricing_rule_and_why_it_is_ordered_t.the_repo_agrees: 182 records are REFUSED and they are counted, not hidden. 51.3% of all records carry an explicit non-claim. That is the highest-value statistic in this census.

what_the_census_changes_about_the_answer: The project is not short of claims. It has 3,228 of them, 20.8 MB of them, across 22+ named benchmark families including SWE-bench, Terminal, OSWorld, LiveBench, HLE, GDPval, CursorBench and Opus55.
Only 10.9% of them declare a passed check. That is the single most important number in this document, because it is measured over the WHOLE population rather than a sample.
5.6% are documented failures. These are assets, not embarrassments -- they are the records that stop the next round repeating a dead end.
51.3% carry an explicit hard non-claim. A project where half of every assertion comes with its own falsification condition is rare, and it is the reason any number in this document can be believed.
34.1% are UNCLASSIFIED, which is honestly a defect: 1,101 records have a status string this census cannot read. That is the largest single improvement available to the governance layer itself.
